wikitext.Babayan, Vahram: {{#fte:person |Born Year=1948|Born Month=August|Born Day=19 |Vahram Ohan Babayan was born in Yerevan on 19 August 1948 to a family of musicians. He has been composing since the age of four. He wrote his first serious compositions at the age of six, and wrote a Symphony for String Orchestra when he was nine. At the age of ten, he wrote the opera The Little House (Տնակ) based on a homonymous fairy tale by Samuil Marshak. In 1968, Vahram Babayan was admitted to the Yerevan Komitas State Conservatory. In 1972, he graduated from the faculty of piano (class of Prof. Vahe Aharonyan), and in 1973, from the faculty of composition (class of Prof. Grigor Yeghiazaryan). Vahram Babayan was a member of the Union of Soviet Composers since 1973, and is a member of the Composers Union of Armenia since 1991. In 1975, Vahram Babayan’s Symphony No. 2, based on a poem by A. Isahakyan, was awarded a prize at the state competition dedicated to the 100th anniversary of A. Isahakyan. In 1982, Vahram Babayan was awarded the Armenian National Young Laureate title. In 1999, 2000, and 2001, he was awarded grants from the Ministry of Culture of Saxony and from Margarethen-Stiftung (Germany). He is a laureate of the Vahan Tekeyan International Prize of the Tekeyan Cultural Association (2009, String Quartet No. 7 ‘Leipzig’). The same year, his Hymn for piano and string orchestra was awarded the World Armenian Congress prize and the Best Composition Award of the Union of Armenians in Russia. In 2011, the composer was awarded the Gold Medal of the Ministry of Culture of the Republic of Armenia. In 2016, Babayan was awarded the laureate of the Best Composition (in the Symphonic Genre) Award by the Composers Union of Armenia for his Symphony No. 5. Vahram Babayan is an Honorary Worker of Art of the Republic of Armenia. He composes in all classical styles and has written six operas: The Stranger (1970), Beethoven’s Letters (1977), Hamlet (1990), Lramlarum (2002), Song about Love and Beauty (2003), The Forty Days of Musa Dagh (2004); four ballets: Pygmalion (1975), Pan (1977), Towards the Light (1995, premiered in Baltimore, USA, in 1995), The Little Prince (1998); two oratorios: Christ Speaks (1991), From Christ’s Life (1995); and a cantata The Year 1915; nine symphonies (1964, 1968, 1972, 1977, 1981, 1985, 1988, 1998, 2009); two symphonic poems and a choreographic poem Antuni; numerous concerti (five for piano); three chamber symphonies; a symphony for percussion; four choral symphonies; works for string orchestra; seven string quartets; a piano quartet; a wind quintet; a piano trio; numerous sonatas for different instruments (seven for piano), vocal cycles, music for children, etc. Vahram Babayan’s works have been performed at various prestigious festivals and concerts in around 40 countries (including the USA, Germany, Austria, Finland, England, Japan, Argentina, Italy, France, Switzerland, Hungary, Romania, and Russia). Vahram Babayan, being a brilliant pianist, has performed in more than ten countries. His works are notable for their psychological depth, unique world view, and philosophy. While his early period is characterized by an avant-garde standpoint, the composer is inclined towards Neoromanticism in his early period, and towards Expressionism at a more mature stage. Several festivals named after Vahram Babayan have been organized in Armenia (the First festival dedicated to the composer’s 50th anniversary being held in 1998, and the Second festival dedicated to the 50th anniversary of his creative activity in 2005). The Vahram Babayan Music Festival in France was founded and held in 2014. Vahram Babayan’s works have been published in France, the UK, Russia, and Armenia. He is the author of numerous articles concerning musical issues. Vahram Babayan has given masterclasses in a number of countries. At present, the composer teaches and is a lecturer-professor at the Yerevan Komitas State Conservatory. |Sex=male |Time Period=Modern |Nationality=Armenian |Biography Link=[https://www.facebook.com/Vahram-Babayan-341967165831688/info/?tab=page_info Facebook] |Picture=Babayan.jpg |Picture Caption= }}

|Extra Information=
* CR Srikanth, also known as Ravi Chandra Srikanth Cherukupalli, is an Indian-born, U.S.-based composer working in Western classical and Romantic chamber forms alongside contemporary genres.
* His catalog includes more than 250 original compositions across solo piano, chamber, orchestral, and hybrid formats, with an opus-numbered classical archive comprising piano works and programmatic chamber fantasias for violin and piano.
* Srikanth's training spans Western classical theory, Carnatic and Hindustani traditions, and film and television composition coursework at Berklee Online (2025).
* His compositional language draws on common-practice harmony, including augmented sixth chords, modal interchange, extended dominant relationships, and imitative counterpoint.
* In April 2026, Srikanth was the featured Guest Composer at the Spring URI Composers' Concert at the University of Rhode Island, in a program directed by Dr. Eliane Aberdam.
* He is the author of ''Bridging Two Traditions: A Working Composer's Handbook on VS Pop Orchestral Thinking'' (2025), and an ASCAP-registered composer and publisher.
* Selected scores are made publicly available on IMSLP for performers, students, and researchers.
}}

wikitext.Delaunay, Samuel:
{{#fte:person
|Alternate Names=
|Born Year=1972|Born Month=08|Born Day=06
|Died Year=|Died Month=|Died Day=
|Nationality=French
|Time Period=Modern
|Picture=Picture-Delaunay,_Samuel.jpg
|Sex=male
|Biography Link=
|Extra Information=Né en 1972, Samuel Delaunay est organiste, flûtiste et compositeur. Professionnellement, il est chef de projet informatique dans une grande société.  En parallèle à des études scientifiques, il débute l’orgue à 20 ans en autodidacte. Il travaille l’improvisation avec Henri-Franck Beaupérin. Plusieurs stages sont l’occasion de pratiquer le répertoire, l’accompagnement et une première approche de l’écriture musicale.  Au conservatoire de Nantes, il suit la classe d’écriture du compositeur Christian Villeneuve et celle d’analyse du chef d’orchestre Jenö Rehak. Une master class avec le compositeur Thierry Escaich est également une étape importante dans cette formation.  Ses compositions donnent une grande place à l'orgue, parfois associé à la flûte. Des pages pour serpents, orchestre ou chœur élargissent cet univers sonore. Les pièces sont souvent organisées sous forme de suites thématiques, explorations de thèmes scientifiques ou poétiques.
}}

|Biography Link=Originario de la ciudad de México, nace el 14 de junio de 1980. Inicia sus estudios de piano y composición en 1998. En el 2000 ingresa a la Escuela Nacional de Música de la UNAM, donde posteriormente concluye la Licenciatura en Composición en el año 2007. De gran importancia en su formación han sido las clases impartidas por Hugo Ignacio Rosales Cruz en Composición, Leonardo Coral en Instrumentación y orquestación, Mario Stern en Análisis musical, Federico Ibarra en Historia y técnicas de la orquestación, Roubina Milner Evguenia en Historia universal de la música y Felipe Ramírez Gil en Historia de la música mexicana. Además de su participación en el curso “El piano en Italia, sus orígenes y desarrollo: Técnica y repertorio en los instrumentos de la época hasta el clasicismo vienés” impartido por el Maestro Carlo Mazzoli, “Los clásicos orquestales del siglo XX” curso impartido por el Maestro Leonardo Coral, Iconografía musical: “El maravilloso mundo de la música visible” curso impartido por la Doctora Roubina Milner Evguenia y las clases magistrales de piano impartidas por el Maestro Piero Rattalino.  Como compositor sus obras se han tocado en las salas de la Escuela Nacional de Música, en el Centro Nacional de las Artes, en la sala “Silvestre Revueltas” y “Angélica Morales” de la Escuela Superior de Música, en la sala “Julián Carrillo” de Radio UNAM, diversos auditorios en Ciudad Universitaria, en el auditorio “Vicente Guerrero” de la Universidad Autónoma Metropolitana Campus Xochimilco, en el auditorio de Extensión Universitaria de la Facultad de Estudios Superiores Cuautitlán, Museo Nacional de San Carlos, Museo Universitario del Chopo, Museo Nacional de Arte, en el Centro Cultural Universitario de la Facultad de Estudios Superiores Acatlán, diversos foros de la República Mexicana y algunas ciudades de Europa. Su música se ha transmitido por radio UNAM y Opus 94, estación del grupo IMER. Desde 2009 hasta la fecha, es profesor de piano y teoría musical en los talleres culturales que se imparten en la Facultad de Estudios Superiores Cuautitlán de la Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México.
|Extra Information=
}}

|Extra Information=Ich bin Musiklehrer im Ruhestand. Im Rahmen meiner Unterrichtstätigkeit komponierte ich viele Werke für den musikalischen Alltagsbetrieb in verschiedenen Besetzungen von der Unterstufe bis zur Oberstufe. Diese sind hier nun öffentlich zugänglich. Stilistisch sind alle Werke als tonal einzuordnen und fordern niemals virtuose Spieltechnik. Atonale, experimentelle Werke im Sinn zeitgenössisscher „musica viva“ fehlen ganz. Um so häufiger dagegen findet sich „crossover“ zur Unterhaltungsmusik, Popularmusik und zum Jazz.

I am a retired music teacher. As part of my teaching work, I composed many works for everyday musical use in various ensembles from lower school to upper school. These are now publicly accessible here. Stylistically, all works can be classified as tonal and never require virtuoso playing technique. Atonal, experimental works in the sense of contemporary “musica viva” are completely missing. However, “crossover” to light music, popular music and jazz is all the more common.
}}

In 1946, after serving in the Signal Corps in the South Pacific during World War II, he took up his first academic position in the Music Department of Kansas State College in Manhattan, Kansas. In 1951, he and his family moved to Rochester, New York, where he earned a PhD in Theory and Composition under Howard Hanson at the Eastman School of Music in 1958. He was a faculty member and then professor in the Theory Department at Eastman from 1955 to 1970, during which time he also served as musical director of the Unitarian Church. He took an early retirement, moving with his wife Bonnie in 1970 to La Veta, Colorado, west of Walsenburg under the Spanish Peaks. wikitext.Green, Anthony:
{{#fte:person
|Alternate Names=Anthony Green
|Born Year=1946|Born Month=01|Born Day=05
|Died Year=2024|Died Month=12|Died Day=20
|Nationality=British
|Time Period=Modern
|Picture=Picture-Green,_Anthony.jpg
|Sex=male
|Biography Link={{More}} Anthony Green was born in 1946 and studied piano with his father, Tanya Polunin and James Gibb, harmony and counterpoint with Anthony Milner, composition also with Anthony Milner and then with Hugh Wood and Melanie Daiken. From 1979 to 1981 he was on a British Council scholarship to Budapest where he studied composition with Zsolt Durkó, piano with Imre Rohmann and Istvan Lantos at the Liszt Academy, where he also studied Bartók-analysis with Ernö Lendvai. Green was a finalist in the BBC Beethoven Chamber Music Competition (1969) and the British Liszt Piano Competition (1976) and has had compositions performed on the BBC and Hungarian Radio.  He taught piano from 1990 at Trinity College of Music until his retirement in 2007. He also lectured on Romantic and Contemporary Music. He started composing at an early age but did not study harmony and counterpoint until the age of 15. Composition was intermittent until his early twenties; Messiaen´s «Vingt regards» inspired him to start composing seriously – other influences were Busoni, particularly the Second Sonatina, and Schönberg, particularly the Op. 33 piano pieces; however, the first piece he acknowledged was not written until 1974-5 («Piano Piece»). He started writing serial music but later used a technique of continuous developing variation of a basic musical idea involving a mathematical permutation of intervals. This is applied in Piano Sonata No. 2 (1985-6), a single movement work lasting 35 minutes, all based on one melodic idea – the work he regards as having found his own voice for the first time. Works include eight piano sonatas (No. 4 entitled «Homage to Sartre»), many shorter piano solos, pieces for piano duet and two pianos, chamber music including 4 works for string quartet, «In Nomine» for string trio, 3 sonatas for violin and piano, a trio for clarinet, cello and piano, pieces for vibraphone and piano, «Pentaptych» and «Little Symphony on the name J. S. Bach» for orchestra, «The Slowworm of Lenty» (J. C. Powys) for soprano, flute, clarinet and cello. Publishers: Modus Music and fonorum. {{MoreEnd}}
|Extra Information=
}}

An Award from the World Armenian Congress for creative achievements, 2009, (“Lord , Have Mercy On Us” choral cycle).
The winner of the ALS International Choral composition competition 2014,(“From “Ts-y to Ts-y”)
The winner of “Best choral composition of the year” 2017, (“Agnus Dei”)
The winner of International Music contest IMelody 2017 (5-th place),(“Ode-Elegy to Varouzhan”). The winner of “Best chamber composition of the year” 2018, (“With the Wing of Hazaran Bird” for Armenian Viola and Harp).
Among her published works: “Neumes” for flute and clarinet, “Aravot Luso or Tagh of the Resurrection” concert for choir and theremin, Antology of Choral compositions dedicated to Armenian Great Genocide, Armenia. “The Labyrinthes of Memory” string quartet, “Ode-Elegy to Varouzhan”, «“A une Dame créole”- Da Vinci Publication, Japan.
She is also a singer of ancient spiritual music-Taghs and sharakans.

*Though Kauffmann was born and died in what is now technically France, the area is known as Alsace, and has changed nationality back and forth many times between French and German. *Teacher at thr ''Rheinische Musikschule'' Cologne, until he was sacked by the Nazis in 1933 for being a „Neutöner“ (progressive). However, he continued to compose for the Cologne radio station under a pseudonym. Finally he found employment at the Strasburg Conservatory in 1940, but was killed in an air raid in 1944. His chamber opera ''Das Perlenhemd ''(1944) was praised by his teacher {{LinkComp|Philipp|Jarnach}} (1892—1982) as "a musical treasure, ..a model for a new style of chamber opera".

He specialized in choral conducting with Werner Pfaff and has attended courses on conducting technique and interpretation held by M. Berrini, N. Corti, P Neumann, G. Graden and H.M. Bäuerle. He directed the choir Mortalisatis, bringing it to the apex of the national panorama. He currently directs the vocal group Caterina Ensemble and the Children’s Choir Antonio Buzzolla at the Conservatory of Adria. As a choral conductor, he has won numerous awards in national competitions, including award for best conductor, twice.
 
As a composer in the competitive field, he has received numerous recognitions on a national and international level. His music is currently performed by choirs all over the world (Italy, Germany, Korea, Latvia, Hungary, Romania, South Africa, The United States, The Philippines, etc.) and is published by Edizioni Pizzicato, Edizioni Carrara, by Edizioni Musicali Europee and by Carus Verlag.
 
Maestro Kirschner is frequently invited as a jury member in choral and composition competitions as well as a lecturer and teacher in choral music specialization courses. He collaborates as pianist and preparatory teacher with the Children’s Choir of the Cesare Pollini Conservatory of Padua. He teaches at the Cesare Pollini Conservatory of Padua and is professor of Choral Conducting technique at the Academy “Righele” of the ASAC Veneto.
}}

wikitext.Latham, Dylan:
{{#fte:person
|Alternate Names=
|Born Year=2000|Born Month=07|Born Day=29
|Died Year=|Died Month=|Died Day=
|Nationality=English
|Time Period=Classical
|Picture=Picture-Latham,_Dylan.jpg
|Sex=male
|Biography Link=
Dylan is 20 years old and lives in Norwich/Manchester. In 2013 He won a scholarship to the Norwich School, winning their music prize all years he attended, and to Pro Corda for their chamber music courses. He attended the NCO for 3 years and in January 2013 he became the youngest recipient of the Michael Badminton Most Promising Strings Award at the Norfolk Young Musician Competition, winning the prize 4 more times since.

Dylan began playing with Rosie Toll when he was 3 ½ through the Suzuki Method. He studied with Alda Dizdari and attended the Junior Guildhall School of Music and Drama from 2012 until 2016 and in 2014 Dylan played solo to a televised 2 million and a full concert hall in Albania. He then did a summer masterclass in Romania with violinist Sherban Lupu and  studied for two years at the Purcell School of Music under the Government’s music and dance scheme, before starting an undergraduate degree in 2018 at the Royal Northern College of Music studying with Jim Clark. He has won the (costume) prize for the RNCM Salon prize so that should say everything you need to know.

He has performed in multiple venues across the UK and Europe and Dylan has been kindly loaned an exceptional instrument from the Michael Badminton trust until he finishes higher education: a Matthew Hardy from 1819.

Dylan hopes pursue a career in chamber playing or coaching in the future, and is currently the first violinist of the Franco Mendes quartet. He enjoys teaching, orchestral playing, and solo playing but says that chamber is what his ideal final goal would be. 

Outside of music Dylan enjoys playing games and film critique, as well as a good old fashioned pint.

|Extra Information=Greatly enjoy writing and playing stupid (usually strings) arrangements so if anyone finds this page then enjoy the fruits of my labours. Extremely questionable composer, passable arranger/transcriber, mainly in it for the memes.

|Extra Information=
*Natalia Pispini (Skvortsova) is a composer of contemporary classical music. She was born in the former USSR. Her professional path consists of piano studies in childhood, musicology studies in college, further musicology studies and specialization in ethnomusicology in conservatory, doctoral degree, fieldwork recordings, work in archives and research laboratories on traditional music, as well as teaching Music, Arts and Humanities courses at various levels. In 2014, she started composing her own music. Some of her music compositions are deeply rooted in Russian cultural heritage. For other works, there is an influence of Western musical traditions, classical and popular. She received great inspirations while living many years in Greece and the Middle East, and that provides her with new ideas, images and tunes. She is passionate about reviewing music composing techniques developed in the past. At the same time, she has a special concern to embrace contemporary approaches, and she likes to experiment with new music structures, scales, rhythms and polyphony schemes. 
}}

|Extra Information= ==Biography==
'''Don Rath Jr.''' (b. 1956) is an American composer, arranger, guitarist, and music publisher born January 14, 1956, in Cincinnati, Ohio. Though largely self-taught in composition, his chamber works have garnered international recognition for their melodic accessibility and emotional depth.

Rath's musical journey began in elementary school with flute-o-phone and cornet, but he found his true voice after discovering the guitar in 1970 during his freshman year of high school. These early experiments with the instrument led to his first compositions and established music as his primary mode of artistic expression.

As a composer, Rath specializes in works for stringed instruments, crafting what he describes as music that "bridges the gap between true classical music and modern song forms." His compositional style blends elements of chamber music, new age, and ambient genres, characterized by memorable melodies, careful attention to instrumental color, and romantic expression ranging from playful to contemplative.

Rath has released four albums: ''Night Wind'', ''Heart Strings'', ''Dawn of a New Day'', and ''Colors of Cello''. His works are available through major digital platforms including Apple Music and YouTube.

For ten years, he served as a screener for the Grammy Awards, an experience that deepened his understanding of contemporary composition and melodic craft. His music has been praised internationally, with listeners noting its thoughtful orchestration, memorable melodies, and stylistic diversity across formats from string quartets to full orchestral arrangements.

|Extra Information=Adolf Reichel (1816-1896) was a Swiss composer of Classical and Neoclassical Romanticism. Born in Tursnitz, West Prussia, he received early music education in Elbing, Thorn, and Danzig, later studying composition under Siegfried Dehn and piano under Ludwig Berger in Berlin. Reichel's career led him to Meiningen, Dresden, Vienna, Bern, Brussels, and Paris, where he befriended notable figures like Frédéric Chopin and George Sand.

Reichel's musical legacy includes over 700 manuscripts, two symphonies, piano concertos, chamber works, and a variety of sacred music and songs. Several of his works were published by prestigious houses such as C.F. Peters and Breitkopf & Härtel. A conservative in musical thought but a versatile composer, Reichel was a highly skilled and productive figure of his time.

Reichel was closely associated with the revolutionary Mikhail Bakunin, supporting him financially and operationally for years. His political convictions led him to move to Bern in 1867, where he became director of the Bern Symphony Orchestra and the Conservatory. Reichel became a Swiss citizen in 1869, establishing a six-generation dynasty of Swiss musicians.

His students included notable names such as August Klughardt and Alexander Taneyev. Despite being largely forgotten for nearly a century, his rediscovered works are now housed in the Bern University of the Arts. His life, intertwined with significant musical and political figures, and his extensive body of work, mark him as a prominent yet underappreciated composer of his era.
}}

|Extra Information=Antonello Rizzella has achieved his degree in piano from the Conservatorio “Dall’Abaco” in Verona and in Choir Direction and Music Didactics from the Conservatorio “G. Verdi” in Como (Italy).
He has also completed the Academic Diploma in Piano under Maestro Cigoli and continued his studies with Maestro Patuzzi.
Antonello Rizzella has studied organ with Maestros Molardi, Raschietti and Bianchi. He has been awarded with he first, second and third prize in many national and international piano or composition competitions.
He is currently teaching Music Disciplines in various Public and Private Institutions near Como (Italy). He is composer for piano teaching (ed.Eurarte, ed.Baci di note), chamber music teaching (SlowayMusicEditions) and choir music teaching (Sonitus and BAM).
He has recorded and released many CDs, two of them with the Chamber Choir of the Conservatorio di Como (Domenico Innominato, director).
He performs as pianist as well as director in numerous northern Italy cities. He is Carimate’s parish regular organist (org. Prestinari 1837), director of the “A. Sala” Choir and of the “Duomo di Como” Children’s Choir.

{{#fte:person
|Born Year=1978|Born Month=12|Born Day=31
|Died Year=|Died Month=|Died Day=
|Time Period=Modern
|Extra Information=*[mailto:music@dwscott.ca Email composer]
|Nationality=South African
|Nationality2=Canadian
|Sex=male
|Biography Link= Douglas Scott was born in Johannesburg, South Africa and started his musical journey at an early age on the piano. At around age ten he took up the flute more seriously and it remained his primary instrument since then. As a teen, he attended the Drakensburg Boys’ Choir School and then the National School of the Arts in Johannesburg, where he had the opportunity to perform as flute soloist with both the Johannesburg Symphony Orchestra and the National Symphony Orchestra. After graduating with a BMus from the University of Pretoria he worked professionally as a flautist and singer for a number of years, performing as bass soloist in the works such as J.S. Bach’s St John’s Passion and Dietrich Buxtehude’s Membra Jesu Nostri. He moved to Singapore while completing his MMus in flute performance through UNISA, where he became involved in amateur dramatics, achieving acclaim in such roles as Van Helsing in Bram Stoker’s Dracula and the Phantom in Stephen Briggs’ and Terry Pratchett’s Maskerade. He has since completed his PhD(music) through the University of the Free State (Odeion)—focusing on a mathematical treatment of the semiotics of musical gesture—and subsequently did postdoctoral year at the Manfred and Penny Conrad Institute for Music Therapy Research (CIMTR) in Waterloo, Canada. Doug is also an active composer and filled various roles (including chairman) with the composer’s organization NewMusicSA, where he curated the 2015 New Music Indaba in Bloemfontein, South Africa. His works so far include “Afrika-dig”, a setting of poems by Lara Kirsten for Mezzo Soprano and large ensemble (with optional dancers), a Keyboard Suite, and a Missa Brevis. Douglas now lives in Fort Frances, Canada, with his wife and two daughters, where he is learning a bit of farming as his ancestors once did while conducting the String Orchestra in the neighbouring US town of International Falls. He enjoys the cultural richness and natural beauty of the region.
|Picture=Scott Douglas Walter.png
}}

wikitext.Witt, Edward:
{{#fte:person
|Born Year=1991|Born Month=12|Born Day=19
|Nationality=American
|Sex=male<!--auto-->
|Time Period=Modern
|Picture=HS1.png}}


Born and raised in the South Hills of Pittsburgh, Ed Witt (b. 1991) began his musical endeavors by taking piano lessons at The Pittsburgh Music Academy in his childhood.  Later taking up the Trumpet and Percussion, he frequently performed in many of the ensembles within the Mt. Lebanon School District, which is recognized nationally for its superior fine arts programs.  He began arranging and composing for several of these groups by his Junior year, namely the highly decorated Mt. Lebanon High School Percussion Ensemble.  Several of these works have received national publication by C. Alan Publications.  Currently under the guidance of Nancy Galbraith, his work attempts to tell stories through colorful, lush harmonies and memorable melodies.  With his knowledge and performance experience on many different instruments, his primary goal is to write idiomatically and effectively for every part, creating an experience that is both enjoyable for an audience to listen to as well as fun for the performers to play.

If you would like to program one of his compositions, or commission a new work, his email is edwardwitt3@gmail.com

You can listen to his work [https://soundcloud.com/ed-witt here]
